hints.content:
$\displaystyle \int_{0}^{4} g(x) \,dx$ is the net area between the curve $y=g(x)$ and the $x$-axis between $x=0$ and $x=4$.

![The graph of function g has the region between the curve and the x-axis, between x = 0 and x = 4, shaded. The portion of the curve at the bottom of the shaded region is concave up, moving downward from (0, 0) to (2, negative 2) then upward to (4, 0).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/494fa9bb3c168b1eda4c13ff764e240c96ac3c76)

Since the curve is $\maroonD{\text{below}}$ the $x$-axis in this interval, the definite integral is $\maroonD{\text{negative}}$.

We can find this area using geometric area formulas. We have half a circle whose radius is $\goldD{2}$.

The area of the entire circle is $\pi\cdot \goldD{2}^2=4\pi$, and half of that is $\dfrac{4\pi}{2}=2\pi$.

The area is $2\pi$ square units, so the integral is $-2\pi$.
